name: Subscriber Count In The Queue Allocation

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Subscriber Count In The Queue Allocation Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

Experiment 11 showed a lock-free subscriber count speeds up every Signal write (−27% unobserved, −9% observed) but cost ~10% on subscription churn because the counter was a second `Arc` cloned into every subscription. Keeping the counter next to the mutex in the queue's single shared allocation keeps the lock-free read while subscriptions capture one `Weak`, as before.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** atomic subscriber count stored in the same allocation as the queue mutex.
**Allowed changes:** `crates/src/primitives/delivery.rs`.
**Forbidden in this experiment:** new callers of `has_subscribers`, drain/enqueue lock changes, Signal changes.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Full lib + integration tests; clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` (scalar-hot), `delivery_complexity` (run twice), `reactive_complexity` vs base. Pass: `signal-set-*` >=10% faster on reruns and fanout regression <5% on reruns.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

Signal write gains of experiment 11 without the subscription-churn cost.
